136: ## Mathematical invariants
137:

139:   fixed logic and its hash-bound verified background supplement. Important
140:   tools remain explicit; ordinary correct elementary reasoning needs no
141:   exhaustive calculation chain. See [background notes](nl0/references/background-notes.md).
142: - Within NL0, each inference uses only its direct inputs, global definitions and explicitly
143:   established in-scope local facts or positively checked node-local background
144:   notes. Notes never add H or repair a substantive gap. Source papers and producer proof bodies do
145:   not fill gaps in a task packet.
146: - Preserve one global mathematical identity while allowing local Lean views.
147:   Actual cross-view conversions need checked proofs. In stage two, the pinned
148:   Mathlib environment is freely available without NL0 M registration.
149: - Shared mathematical extraction is a bounded local change at translation entry.
150:   Review its new producer and substitution cuts; inherit unchanged evidence.
151:   Freeze the revised NL0 before final IR and worker packets.
152: - Local conditional bodies may run concurrently. Assembly must discharge every
153:   internal dependency with an actual checked proof; conditional checks alone
154:   are not a final result.
155: - The independent pre-freeze review checks every E and complete P, including
156:   hypotheses, quantifiers and relevant definitions. Final machine Audit B checks

158:   Supply short direct/equivalent correspondence explanations. Check actual Lean
159:   closure and trust, without a Mathlib-to-NL0 use ledger.
160:   Neither author notes nor a compiler pass are semantic approval.
161: - Stop on a judged substantive mathematical gap. Ordinary expansion and local
162:   verifiable corrections remain allowed. Difficulty or elapsed time does not
163:   establish that a mathematical claim is false.

1: # Audit A: per-object natural-language verification
2: 
3: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:begin -->
4: ## Shared mathematical acceptance requirements
5: 
6: Contract version: `nl0-audit-a-8`.
7: 
8: This section is the single authority for what an accepted NL0 must satisfy.
9: Authoring instructions explain how to meet it; the audit checks these same
10: requirements. The table IDs also name executable coverage groups. Detailed
11: definitions in self-containment, logical rules and external-theorem review are
12: annexes to these requirements, not alternative permission policies.
13: 
14: | ID | Review group | Author evidence group | Requirement |
15: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
16: | `target` | package | original_context_note | Preserve the original target, every original H, quantifier, domain, range, normalization, endpoint and supplied core proof route. Parameters name ambient data; they cannot hide an H or a desired conclusion. |
17: | `definitions` | package | original_context_note | Give each global object one complete typed definition and each local object a legitimate scoped introduction. Prove or directly assume every construction guard before use. Defining an object grants none of its properties. |
18: | `sources` | package | original_context_note | Every selected M/E has an explicit faithful full statement and verified primary/native identity, context and hypotheses. Native typeclass premises are mathematical premises too. Record inaccessible checks as UNVERIFIED; they do not support an unqualified whole-proof pass. |
19: | `structure` | package | original_context_note | H/E/M are the only proposition roots. Every N/P has one producer, every retained non-H node lies in P's AND dependency closure, and every local proof uses its actual direct inputs. Keep every original H, including an unused H, and report which are unused. An ancestor is not automatically an input. |
20: | `statement_closure` | closure | output_notes | Every input and exported N/P states all formulas, quantifiers, conditions and semantic identifications needed by its consumers. A map or identity only present in the producer's body is unavailable to another node. Original text, equation labels and external notation cannot supply content. |
21: | `object_closure` | closure | declaration_check | Reverse-check actual object occurrences against global, statement-bound or local declarations. Types, domains, witness existence, first/last use and parameter dependencies agree. A name in a ledger is not an introduction or existence proof. |
22: | `dependency_closure` | closure | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Ground factual uses in direct H/E/M/N, earlier in-scope local proofs, permitted elementary reasoning, or positively checked background notes under verified-background-1. Inspect actual prose and conditions; an inventory is not its proof. |
23: | `inputs` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Direct input statements are faithfully instantiated with compatible objects and assumptions. An internal input exports exactly its stated conclusion, not its producer's unexported facts. |
24: | `argument` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Establish every output clause at ordinary rigorous natural-language granularity. Check material domains, limits, regularity, uniformity, integrability, signs, constants and degeneracies. Correct routine compression needs no exhaustive elementary calculation chain. |
25: | `dependency_accounting` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Every explicit input has a real role. Record eligible omitted basic library uses as verified background notes instead of rejecting solely for missing M accounting. No unverified source, extra H, core proof or project lemma can hide in prose, definitions or typeclasses. |
26: | `output` | inference | output_notes | The proved conclusion is the exact complete exported statement under its stated hypotheses, including all consumer-needed representations and identifications. Never weaken the target or strengthen an H to close the graph. |
27: | `scope` | inference | dependency_and_local_assumption_check | Introduce and discharge temporary assumptions inside arguments. Close implications, cases, negations and quantifiers correctly; no witness or local assumption escapes. Original hypotheses remain explicit H inputs. |
28: | `applicability` | inference | source_application_check | For every actual M/E use, give the exact substitution and a direct input or displayed earlier derivation for every premise, plus any proved bridge to the claimed conclusion. Saying that a condition holds is not grounds for it. |
29: 
30: ### Scope of the same requirements
31: 
32: Global review checks the original target/H, source authenticity and complete
33: graph: H/E/M are its roots, and each N/P has its producer in that graph.
34: Its source judgments establish identity, full-statement fidelity and source
35: conditions; they do not re-prove each consumer's application. Its structure
36: judgment checks the actual AND graph and declared producer/input boundaries,
37: not whether a later packet reviewer has already returned PASS. Conditional
38: packet review owns each actual substitution, premise discharge, local proof
39: and output under those checked source statements. Final acceptance joins
40: all required source, structure and packet judgments; none replaces another.
41: Unfinished downstream assessment is not a reason to mark an already assessed
42: source identity or structural graph uncertain. Genuine source uncertainty
43: still blocks final acceptance. These assignments also govern author checks.
44: An original H remains explicitly present even when the proof does not use it;
45: report that unused condition. Do not invent a use or delete it to force graph
46: reachability. Selected E/M and internal N remain in the actual target closure.
47: Conditional packet replay has a different input boundary. Its task is the
48: implication from its explicitly supplied H/E/M/N statements to its output;
49: these statements are conditional premises. An input N is not a new global
50: root. Its producer body is intentionally absent and is neither required nor
51: available during this local check. Do not fail a valid conditional derivation
52: because its input theorem's producer or original source is outside the packet;
53: global review verifies source identity and producer membership, while the
54: producer's own packet review checks its proof. Conversely, do not import an absent N, an
55: ancestor's unexported fact or a theorem not present in the packet.
56: For example, a supplied N stating A and B permits deriving A by conjunction
57: elimination, without re-proving N. Having no such input does not permit
58: asserting A. The local requirements still check the complete actual argument,
59: all source-application premises, declarations, guards and discharged scopes.
60: These scopes are also the scopes of the author's corresponding self-checks.
61: 
62: The common elementary layer is the controller's `elementary-language-4` profile:
63: equality, unfolding supplied definitions, routine finite semiring/ring/field
64: arithmetic, elementary ordered-field inequalities and explicit finite sums.
65: It grants no calculus, integral identity, measure, compactness, basis,
66: localization or tensor theorem. Use a verified input or a displayed local proof
67: for substantive facts. The verified-background admission rule below additionally
68: permits positively checked ordinary library facts without prior author M registration.
69: No theorem needs to be re-proved if its exact permitted source
70: and application already supply it. The schema describes representation; it
71: does not extend mathematical permissions. The core syntax table contains no
72: subject-specific vocabulary. Problem objects and notation use their own typed
73: parameter, definition or local declarations, in any mathematical field.
74: 
75: The fixed profile is controller-owned. A packet/spec's `logic.calculations`,
76: `logic.primitives`, or prose claiming extra permissions is data to check
77: against that profile, never a second authority. Ordinary valid elementary
78: inferences may be compressed: do not demand a displayed chain for every midpoint
79: bound, rearrangement or elementary construction. Check that the conclusion
80: actually follows with the required signs and domains. A substantive missing
81: argument is not made elementary by naming its conclusion.
82: 
83: ### Verified background admission: verified-background-1
84: 
85: Keep all review dimensions. At A4 an omitted routine elementary explanation or
86: basic pinned-mathlib fact may PASS after positive mathematical checking. Record
87: useful routine completion or omitted library use in a node-local background note:
88: ID, exact argument location, precise fact, actual local condition grounds,
89: reviewer's justification, checked library evidence where applicable, optional
90: Lean hint. Use `record_background_note`; for library notes first obtain actual
91: `probe_background` evidence. The source and application are checked now; Lean
92: syntax, representations, coercions and proof terms remain translation work.
93: 
94: Eligibility requires a correct local standard step, all conditions already
95: available, no new hypothesis and no substantial new proof or changed route.
96: Do not replace core tools, missing project results, source uncertainty, witness
97: existence or unjustified limit exchanges by notes. A familiar name or guessed
98: library availability is insufficient. A recorded note contains no unresolved
99: mathematical TODO. Do not log every associativity step or duplicate explicit M.
100: 
101: Authors explicitly register important tools, write ordinary rigorous arguments
102: and self-check under this same policy; they need not anticipate every tiny M
103: use. An auditor can transparently complete routine accounting without returning
104: the whole NL0 for a rewrite. The accepted authority is immutable author NL0 plus
105: the hash-bound audit/notes supplement. It is not an old-policy claim that every
106: dependency was explicitly registered by the author.
107: 
108: Fresh local reviewers may consult only logged read-only pinned-mathlib sources
109: in addition to their own packet and Yui rules. Preserve successful source probes
110: and actual tool readback evidence. This is
111: `fresh_packet_with_verified_background`, not old `fresh_packet_only` replay.
112: No other task, project proof, original/ancestor proof, repair history or owner
113: hint is permitted. Unverified facts remain FAIL/UNVERIFIED as appropriate.
114: Display PASS with background notes when present, retaining their count. The
115: supplement is mandatory translation input; none of its facts may become an
116: unproved Lean assumption. See [background notes](background-notes.md).
117: 
118: A calculation label alone does not establish the existence of a canonical
119: decomposition, normal form, extremizer, basis or structural identification.
120: Give the actual construction and grounds for its required properties and
121: completion, or supply a verified source with its actual application. Before
122: declaring a mathematical obstruction, check the full quantified definition
123: and the direction of the claimed bounds. One feasible value alone does not
124: establish an extremal value. A failed attempted argument is not by itself
125: evidence against the supplied proof.
126: 
127: Unfolding an explicitly supplied definition and displaying its logical
128: consequence is a local derivation; it does not need a separate source theorem
129: merely because that consequence has a familiar name. Conversely, a familiar
130: name without the required definition, premises and derivation supplies no
131: fact. Check the actual argument and identify the specific unsupported step;
132: do not replace that check with a blanket objection to a named result.
133: Distinguish a genuinely partial construction from an explicitly total
134: operation: its stated type/convention controls which existence guards are
135: needed, and totality alone grants no intended analytic property.
136: 
137: Authors construct arguments and their evidence together, then report their
138: own actual check outcomes. An explicitly unresolved or unperformed check
139: prevents release as a complete artifact. Finishing a checklist, retrieving a
140: source, passing a structural gate or asserting that conditions hold proves
141: none of the mathematical requirements. Audit A remains an independent actual
142: judgment and can find an omission the author did not recognize.
143: <!-- yui-nl0-acceptance:end -->
144: 
145: ## Auditor execution protocol
146: 
147: The sections below implement the shared requirements. Reviewer identity,
148: fresh packet replay, negative controls, evidence capture and verdict handling
149: are auditor/controller duties; they are not extra mathematical facts for an
150: NL0 author. Mathematical FAIL findings identify the applicable shared table
151: ID and the exact unsupported implication. If the permission boundary itself
152: is ambiguous, disclose that ambiguity rather than silently raising the bar.
153: 
154: Use [self-containment](self-containment.md) and the
155: [audit template](../templates/audit-a.md). New acceptance requires spec/graph
156: v2 and audit v3. Historical PASS records do not satisfy these requirements.
157: 
158: This audit does not use a successful project Lean build as evidence that the
159: NL proof is correct. Querying pinned mathlib for source signatures is allowed;
160: reusing the target's historical Lean proof/verdict requires explicit disclosure
161: and does not establish an independent NL audit.
162: 
163: ## A0. Freeze and disclose
164: 
165: Read the original problem and independently check `spec.json`: target,
166: quantifiers, all H roots, parameter ranges, definitions, representatives,
167: normalization, endpoint conventions, and one-target scope. No H may originate
168: from the proof writer's desired conclusion. Audit target semantics, not just
169: hash equality. Record reviewer/carrier, shared context, read artifacts, and
170: whether any reference solution was seen. Read the canonical graph, not only
171: its generated Markdown. Bind the receipt to spec/graph hashes.
172: Generate the exhaustive global index with
173: `python3 nl0/scripts/nl0.py overview nl0.json --spec spec.json --out global-overview.json`.
174: It preserves every actual H (including unused or late-appended H), full global
175: statements/definitions and dependency edges with canonical pointers and hashes.
176: Read this inventory before claiming a node/condition is absent; a partial line
177: page cannot establish absence. The index supplies no verdict and does not
178: replace inspection of the relevant canonical proof and primary-source content.
179: The clean test adapter uses this same core generator, not a separate inventory
180: or mathematical standard.
181: Original-problem/source fidelity and local proof validity are separate tasks.
182: The original text may be read for target and citation checks; it may not fill
183: missing content during per-R packet-only replay. Record the actual boundary.
184: Check that original conditions really are H nodes, rather than predicates
185: hidden in a globally visible parameter type. A prime/nonzero condition,
186: characteristic constraint, range or equation must not become available to an
187: R with empty inputs through that encoding. Matching the full closed theorem
188: alone does not establish correct per-R H availability.
189: 
190: ## A1. Definitions and notation
191: 
192: For each D record a verdict with a concrete explanation. Check unique meaning,
193: type/domain, global versus local binding, definition dependencies, construction
194: or existence prerequisites, and applicability at every use. A guarded symbol
195: must not supply its own prerequisite. Record arbitrary choices, parameter
196: dependencies, and equivalence to the original definition. No project theorem
197: may hide as a definition, record field, predicate, or typeclass assumption.
198: 
199: Reverse-check every actual mathematical object occurrence against a legitimate
200: declaration. Inspect local introduction position, first use, type/domain,
201: basis and end scope. Input-bound variables are not free locals; witnesses need
202: proved existence. Merely checking registered symbol names misses unregistered
203: ones. Definitions cannot smuggle properties or extra ancestor statements.
204: 
205: ## A2. Sources
206: 
207: For each M read the pinned official file and a successful full Lean signature
208: probe, not merely a `#check` name or a search result. Confirm declaration kind,
209: restatement, all implicit/typeclass assumptions, source hashes and commit,
210: relevant axioms, and suitability of scalar fields/domains. Library definitions
211: are not theorems. These source checks belong to global review; each using R's
212: packet review inspects its actual application mappings and premise discharge.
213: 
214: For each E execute all nine requirements in
215: [external-theorem review](external-theorems.md). Give separate evidence-bound
216: verdicts for document identity, occurrence of the actual result, faithful
217: statement, complete surrounding context, and version/source eligibility.
218: Record every actual application separately in its using R, including repeated
219: uses of E in one R; packet review checks those applications. Global review
220: checks the source identity and statement. Source existence, exact citation and valid application are separate
221: obligations. Substantive transformations require an N proof. Do not infer any
222: of these verdicts from a historical audit or a successful Lean build.
223: 
224: ### Paywalled or inaccessible primary text
225: 
226: Search public sources using the title, DOI and authors: Google, arXiv,
227: author manuscripts, institutional repositories and accessible publisher text.
228: Use actual source readback, not a search snippet. A different readable version
229: must be identified honestly and checked against its own statement and context.
230: A page requiring JavaScript, login, payment or human verification is an access
231: limitation; do not bypass it or treat the page as the theorem text.
232: 
233: When the primary text remains inaccessible, follow the exact
234: [conditional-source contract](conditional-sources.md). A complete statement
235: actually quoted in a supplied secondary source may remain an explicit E
236: assumption with a bound access-failure record. Keep its source review and
237: unperformed citation checks UNVERIFIED. Every mathematical/application check

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This is the detailed meaning of Audit A's `statement_closure`,
4: `object_closure` and `dependency_closure` requirements. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound verified background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under verified-background-1, local review may additionally verify routine
25: pinned-mathlib facts using logged read-only queries and record them in the
26: receipt. They join this R's effective dependencies, without new H or a graph
27: rewrite. See [background notes](background-notes.md). Mathematical uncertainty
28: still blocks; ordinary correct elementary compression alone does not.
29: 
30: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
31: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
32: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
33: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
34: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
35: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
36: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
37: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
38: 
39: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
40: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
41: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
42: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
43: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
44: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
45: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
46: 
47: ## Object closure
48: 
49: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
50: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
51: 
52: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
53:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
54:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
55:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
56:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
57: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
58:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
59:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
60: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
61:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
62:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
63:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
64: 
65: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
66: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
67: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
68: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
69: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
70: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
71: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
72: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
73: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
74: 
75: ## Dependency closure
76: 
77: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
78: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
79: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible omitted basic library uses are
80: recorded as verified audit notes in the effective dependency ledger. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
81: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
82: 
83: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
84: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
85: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
86: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
87: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
88: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
89: 
90: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
91: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
92: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
93: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
94: theorem. Such facts need a declared input or an actual local derivation.
95: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
96: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
97: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
98: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
99: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
100: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
101: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
102: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
103: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
104: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
105: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
106: 
107: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
108: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
109: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
110: 
111: ## Operational acceptance
112: 
113: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
114:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
115: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
116:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
117:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
118:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
119: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
120:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
121: 4. Perform a fresh local replay with disclosed controlled background lookup. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
122:    and that packet plus logged pinned-mathlib queries, without original proof,
123:    other R bodies, author review
124:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
125:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
126:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
127:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
128:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
129:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
130:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
131:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
132:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
133: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
134:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
135:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
136:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
137:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
138:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
139: 
140: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
141: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
142: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
143: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
144: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
145: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
146: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
147: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

16: ## Authority and semantics
17: 
18: The isolated authoring carrier offers `check_draft` and `submit_draft`, taking
19: an `artifact` JSON object directly. Prefer these to the compatible older
20: `artifact_json` string wrappers: an additional string-encoding layer is not
21: part of the mathematical format. Both routes execute identical checks.
22: 
23: `spec.json` freezes the original full theorem, the conclusion under its declared
24: parameters/hypotheses, the exact H list, global definition pairs, logic policy,
25: source-input hashes, and Lean/mathlib pins. A human must confirm that this
26: specification matches the original problem; string equality cannot establish
27: semantic fidelity. `nl0.json` references this spec by its SHA256 and duplicates
28: none of its definitions or H statements. One separate spec is required per
29: target. Multiple-target decomposition is outside version 2.
30: 
31: Read a derived proposition as a theorem under the original parameters and the
32: H nodes actually used on its derivation path. All additional free variables are
33: locally quantified in its statement; there are no ambient undeclared claims.
34: An unused original H is allowed and reported; do not silently strengthen or
35: weaken the frozen theorem. E/M results retain their general signatures; apply
36: them through explicit bindings and hypothesis checks in the inference.
37: 
38: Graph vertices are propositions and inferences. Edges are generated only as
39: `input proposition -> inference -> output proposition`. An inference requires
40: all inputs. List order is presentation only: a dependency may occur later in
41: the JSON array, provided the graph admits a topological order. Actual circular
42: dependencies, unknown IDs, and disconnected retained branches fail.
43: 
44: The isolated authoring carrier also reports a hash-bound machine checkpoint of
45: its latest own draft and actual structural result. After a context reset, resume
46: that candidate with `read_draft`/`base_candidate`; do not claim no draft exists or
47: restart the frozen input accidentally. The checkpoint grants no Audit A verdict.

49: ## Specification fields
50: 
51: Use [the authoring template](../templates/authoring.md) and the complete
52: [model-visible submission example](../templates/submission-example.md). The
53: example explains metadata placeholders and local-witness accounting; it is not
54: a benchmark or proof certification. Required top-level spec fields are:
55: 
56: - `format_version: 2`, `case_id`, `full_target`, `conclusion` (nonempty strings);
57: - `parameters`: records `{symbol, type}`; parameter symbols reserve global names.
58:   Give ambient data types/structures only. Original conditions, ranges and
59:   equations belong in H, not in parameter refinements that would be visible
60:   to every R;
61: - `hypotheses`: records `{id: Hddd, statement, origin}` extracted before authoring;
62: - `definitions`: records `{id: Dddd, symbol, definition, type, depends_on,
63:   requires, binders, objects}`. Each symbol has exactly one global meaning. `depends_on` lists
64:   earlier/resolvable D IDs and is acyclic. `requires` lists proved H/N IDs that
65:   must already be available whenever the definition is used;
66: - `logic`: `{classical: boolean, rules: [names], calculations: [fixed IDs],
67:   primitives: [{symbol, type, meaning}]}`. In the clean author tool, omit
68:   `calculations` and `primitives` to bind the controller's fixed language profile.
69:   Optional calculation IDs are `equality`, `definitions`, `finite_algebra`,
70:   `finite_order`, `finite_sums`. Optional primitive selections may be
71:   `{symbol: ...}`; the controller validates selections and binds the complete
72:   core syntax with exact type/meaning (numerals, number systems and empty-set/top
73:   notation). This is not a subject vocabulary or a list of allowed theorems. A new
74:   Audit A requires the bound metadata. Author-defined permission descriptions
75:   and conflicting primitive meanings are rejected, not silently accepted;
76: - `pins`: `{lean_version, mathlib_commit, mathlib_root}`; the root is a local
77:   locator, the version/commit are scientific identifiers;
78: - `inputs`: evidence records `{path, sha256}` for the original problem/proof.

80: The exact machine identifiers permitted in `logic.rules` and inference `rules`
81: are `direct`, `modus_ponens`, `implication_introduction`, `negation_introduction`,
82: `contradiction_classical`, `case_elimination`, `forall_introduction`,
83: `exists_elimination`, and `natural_induction`. Describe algebra/analysis in the
84: actual proof text; it is not a new trusted logical rule. These identifiers
85: describe proof packaging, not a substitute for establishing the implication.
86: 
87: The `elementary-language-4` profile in `nl0/scripts/foundations.py` permits
88: displayed finite algebra/order calculations and ordinary logic. Its core syntax
89: contains no domain-specific vocabulary. Objects and notation from any subject
90: are parameters, D definitions or scoped locals, with explicit meaning, type and
91: dependencies; they cannot be hidden in primitives. Recognizable notation grants
92: no identity, existence or regularity. No global dictionary extension is needed
93: to represent a new subject.
94: For every substantive fact still register an E/M input or give its local proof.

96: Older saved specifications retain their original bytes and symbol metadata for
97: read-only inspection under their recorded runtime. Starting a new Audit A under
98: this profile requires current canonical metadata: remove obsolete domain
99: primitive entries, declare any objects they actually supplied, and validate
100: the resulting source again. A new profile does not upgrade an old receipt.

102: Definitions may be globally visible but guarded. Example: “K is the unique
103: fixed curve from N008” requires N008 before K is used. N008 itself must state
104: existence using the previously defined space/operator, without assuming K.
105: Proof prerequisites must be direct inference inputs in v2;
106: the output being proved cannot discharge its own definition prerequisite.
107: Definition prerequisites of input/output statements are checked too.

109: ## Proposition fields
110: 
111: Every proposition has `id`, `kind`, the complete `statement`, `definitions`
112: (D IDs), `binders`, and `objects`:
113: 
114: - `binders`: `{symbol, type}` records for statement-bound variables. These do
115:   not introduce free variables in a consuming R. Register actual nested scope
116:   in the statement; alpha-rename to avoid global shadowing.
117: - `objects`: distinct names of mathematical objects actually used in the
118:   statement, from frozen parameters/primitives, referenced D closure or these
119:   binders. A D also has these fields for its defining expression.

121: These are inventories, not a parser-generated list. Audit A must find omitted
122: objects by reading actual prose/formulas. Export all formulas and conditions;
123: another N ID or an original equation number cannot replace their content.

125: | kind | ID | Producer | Additional fields |
126: |---|---|---|---|
127: | `hypothesis` | Hddd | none | exactly matches frozen H statement |
128: | `mathlib` | Mddd | none | `source` record below |
129: | `external` | Eddd | none | `source` record below |
130: | `internal` | Nddd | exactly one | `origin` locating source or explaining added bridge |

148: The clean probe resolves genuine aliases to their canonical kernel name and
149: discovers the actual defining module. A requested module is only a locator
150: hint; its correction is recorded, never silently treated as source evidence.
151: Native type printing (and the legacy `#check @declaration` probe) preserves the complete outer telescope,
152: including implicit/typeclass conditions, using ordinary notation for nested
153: structure applications. Recursive expansion of inherited structure arguments
154: is unnecessary; omitted hypotheses or ellipsis are not permitted. The actual

1: # External-theorem review: required Audit A standard
2: 
3: Apply this standard to every retained E and every actual use of E in an R.
4: An E keeps the full source theorem; a derived specialization or substantive
5: translation is an internal N. Use the data contract's audit version 2. These
6: are reviewer obligations: a filled record or matching hash cannot establish
7: that a publication or a mathematical assertion is genuine.
8: 
9: ## 1. Document identity
10: 
11: Obtain and read the actual primary document. Match author, title, source kind,
12: publication/release information and exact edition/version to its provenance.
13: Record a traceable original source, retrieval date, local document and hash.
14: A search snippet, model answer, secondary citation, or functioning DOI/URL
15: alone does not establish identity. Books, papers and reliable preprints can
16: qualify; a DOI and journal publication are not universal requirements. Record
17: the source category and grounds for treating it as an admissible source.
18: 
19: For missing originals, follow [ordered source retrieval](source-retrieval.md):
20: arXiv, Google full text, Google DOI discovery and confirmed-DOI Sci-Hub lookup.
21: Use normal browser readback when needed; unresolved access and verification
22: failures remain recorded. Then use the [conditional-source
23: procedure](conditional-sources.md) for unavailable text. Unavailable checks remain UNVERIFIED. A complete explicit
24: secondary statement can support a disclosed conditional run, not an ordinary
25: source-verification PASS.
26: 
27: ## 2. Occurrence of the result
28: 
29: Locate the claimed result in that document and version. Record theorem,
30: lemma, proposition or corollary label and page/section/paragraph/equation as
31: available; unnumbered results require an equally reproducible locator. Retain
32: the relevant primary text or a precise readback record bound to the document.
33: If the cited document merely points elsewhere without actually stating the
34: claimed result, follow and correct the source. An explicitly stated theorem in
35: an authoritative exposition can be cited as such; record its proof attribution
36: without claiming to have audited the referenced proof recursively.
37: Distinguish proved assertions from conjectures, questions, heuristics and
38: numerical observations. Preserve every condition of a conditional result.
39: 
40: ## 3. Statement fidelity
41: 
42: Compare the original full statement with the E statement, explicitly covering
43: objects, domains, scalar fields, spaces, hypotheses, regularity, quantifier
44: order, parameter intervals/endpoints, degeneracies, constant dependencies and
45: the exact conclusion (including a.e./everywhere, topology, uniformity,
46: existence/uniqueness and local/global scope). Record the notation map.
47: Faithful mathematical meaning, not word-for-word copying, is required.
48: Alpha-renaming is allowed. Never turn forall-x-exists-C_x into exists-C-forall-x.
49: 
50: ## 4. Complete context and definitions
51: 
52: Read the surrounding standing assumptions, definitions and conventions that
53: govern the result, including referenced context needed to understand it.
54: Capture any omitted chapter-wide hypotheses and normalization of measures,
55: norms, transforms, signs or scales. Map the source objects to the global D
56: ledger. Do not hide a condition outside the proof graph. A substantive
57: conversion requires an N proof; a renamed symbol is not that proof.
58: 
59: ## 5. Version status and source eligibility
60: 
61: Match every locator and statement to the chosen version. Check available
62: primary version histories, corrections, errata or withdrawal information at
63: the recorded date and scope. Record relevant findings and their effect;
64: explain use of an older version. Absence of a discovered correction is not
65: a guarantee that none exists. Unresolved conflicts remain UNVERIFIED.
66: Never import the target, an unproved project lemma, or a circular dependency
67: as E. Previously proved project modules require an expanded graph or a
68: versioned proof handoff. Do not attribute a combination of sources and a
69: project bridge to a single published theorem. A conjecture-dependent theorem
70: must retain that condition, which must be supplied legitimately at application.
71: 
72: ## 6. Every actual application
73: 
74: Give each actual E application an inference-local A ID. The same E applied
75: twice with different bindings has two A records, even within the same R.
76: For each A inspect the parameter/object bindings, prove every source
77: hypothesis from declared inputs or displayed local derivations, check types,
78: definitions and parameter ranges, identify substantive bridge N nodes, and
79: verify the resulting conclusion supports R's output. Record the evidence for
80: each individual hypothesis. “The theorem applies” is not a mapping.
81: Do not add an unproved hypothesis to close an application. An E passed at its
82: source does not automatically pass at any application site.
83: 
84: ## 7. Ownership of derived work
85: 
86: Put substantive specialization, scaling, change of normalization/domain/space/
87: norm/representation, combinations of sources, and prerequisite lemmas in N.
88: Each N lists its actual E/M/H/earlier-N inputs and its argument. Do not enlarge
89: the quoted theorem. Explicit elementary calculations and logical instantiation
90: may remain inside R; justify them rather than imposing needless graph nodes.
91: 
92: ## 8. Separate decisions and reproducible evidence
93: 
94: For each E write five separate review records: `literature_identity`,
95: `result_location`, `statement_fidelity`, `context_completeness`, and
96: `version_and_eligibility`. Each contains verdict, concrete notes and hashed
97: evidence. The first three must never be merged into one blanket PASS.
98: For each R/A write separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews,
99: the source ID and the proved bridge IDs. Record actual reviewer, carrier,
100: shared context and reference material read. Self-audit is not independent.
101: 
102: Use PASS only after the check was performed with adequate evidence; FAIL for
103: an established mismatch/omission/invalid application; UNVERIFIED when necessary
104: evidence is missing. Inaccessible text does not establish nonexistence. An
105: established absence of the claimed result in the cited source is a FAIL.
106: Retain failed records and the exact reason, source location and affected nodes.
107: 
108: ## 9. Acceptance, invalidation and trust boundary
109: 
110: Every retained E check and every application must PASS before the graph can
111: receive DRAFT-AUDIT-PASSED. A load-bearing FAIL blocks acceptance. Source-verification UNVERIFIED can
112: support only the explicitly qualified continuation above; other unresolved
113: mathematical checks still block it. Ordinary whole-proof acceptance requires
114: every retained check to pass. Never replace a
115: missing verification with a historical audit or a Lean build. Changes to the
116: source/version, statement, definitions, bindings or condition proofs invalidate
117: affected reviews; bind the replacement whole receipt to new canonical hashes.
118: 
119: An inaccessible source suspends its citation verification, not the rest of
120: the workflow: continue available checks and explicitly conditional reasoning,
121: then report the unfinished citation checks and the UNVERIFIED overall audit
122: outcome. Descendants can be proved only relative to the explicit E assumption; the
123: whole result cannot receive an unconditional pass based on that source, and source inaccessibility alone is not a finding of mathematical error.
124: 
125: List all external dependencies in the final verdict. This audit is relative
126: to those identified theorems; it does not independently reprove their published
127: proofs or establish a Lean proof of E. Mechanical checks establish record
128: coverage and byte consistency, not authenticity or mathematical correctness.

1: # Package local reasoning as true theorem nodes
2: 
3: The main graph has only E/M/H source propositions. A temporary assumption is
4: an argument-local device, never a trusted graph vertex. Every exported N/P is
5: a complete claim under the frozen original context. The audit inspects the
6: local derivation; surface implication syntax alone is insufficient.
7: The complete [neutral JSON example](../templates/quantified-implication-example.md)
8: shows an arbitrary binder, a local antecedent, its discharge and the full
9: quantified output. Follow this accounting rather than silently granting a
10: property in a local object's type.
11: 
12: ## Implication and contradiction
13: 
14: To prove `X -> Y`, introduce X inside one argument, derive Y from the declared
15: inputs, then discharge X into the antecedent. Output `X -> Y`, not Y. To use Y
16: unconditionally later, supply an actually proved X and apply implication
17: elimination. A local X and a proved X are not the same proof object.
18: 
19: To prove `not X`, derive false under local X and discharge X by negation
20: introduction. To prove P by classical contradiction, first produce the complete
21: theorem `not P -> false` (equivalently `not not P`), then apply the fixed
22: classical rule. A single R may combine the operations if every local assumption
23: is accounted for. No classical double-negation elimination under an
24: intuitionistic-only policy.
25: 
26: Example graph: N1 `(not P -> Q)`, N2 `not Q`, R1 outputs N3
27: `(not P -> false)`, R2 outputs P. The argument of R1 locally assumes not P,
28: applies N1 and N2, and closes that assumption. No `not P` root is added.
29: The fallacy “assume P, obtain P, discharge and output P” fails: its valid output
30: would be `P -> P`.
31: 
32: ## Cases
33: 
34: From an already proved `A or B or C`, obtain a common target Q by complete
35: conditional lemmas `A -> Q`, `B -> Q`, `C -> Q`, then disjunction elimination.
36: Alternatively prove `not A`, `not B` and conclude C using the original
37: disjunction. Eliminating A/B without a proved exhaustive disjunction cannot
38: establish C. A branch producing false can produce the common target by false
39: elimination; it does not make false an unconditional source proposition.
40: 
41: Proof bodies may contain all branches locally instead of exporting every
42: branch lemma. Check coverage, identical target/ambient context, and the absence
43: of sibling-branch fact/witness leakage. Introduce/discharge each branch-local
44: assumption in its actual scope.
45: 
46: ## Quantifiers, witnesses, and induction
47: 
48: For universal introduction use an arbitrary variable, then close its binder.
49: It must not occur free in an undischarged extra assumption. If the intended
50: theorem has a premise H(x), retain it in the quantified implication.
51: 
52: For existential elimination start from a proved existence statement, choose a
53: fresh local witness with exactly its stated properties, and prove a conclusion
54: independent of that witness's private identity. A witness depending on n does
55: not yield one witness valid for every n. Do not turn a local witness into a
56: globally available constant without a legitimate, recorded construction.
57: 
58: For natural-number induction prove the base and the complete step
59: `forall n, Q(n) -> Q(n+1)` and use induction to conclude `forall n, Q(n)`.
60: The induction hypothesis is local to the step; there is no circular graph edge.
61: If the step invokes the hypothesis at a transformed point s, include
62: `forall s` in the induction invariant. Well-founded induction needs the exact
63: well-founded relation/decrease justification; the word “induct” is not enough.
64: 
65: ## Local notation
66: 
67: Global symbols are reserved. Local binders can repeat across separate nodes
68: or separate binding scopes in a node, but cannot shadow a global symbol.
69: `sum_{k=1}^N` binds k only in that expression. Source theorem dummy variables
70: are alpha-renamed locally, not registered as a new global object each time.
71: Freshness, witness dependencies, constant uniformity, and binder scope are
72: mathematical audit obligations; a list of names does not verify the formula.
73: In v2, local declarations identify introduction kind/basis and inclusive S
74: start/end positions. An input-bound name needs instantiation; a witness needs
75: an actual existence premise. Local F facts record their complete statement,
76: statement-local binders, used objects and remaining assumptions. Neither a
77: fact nor a chosen witness may escape its scope. The checker accounts for
78: declared scopes; Audit A must also inspect the actual quantifier reasoning.

1: # Verified background notes
2: 
3: Audit A's shared acceptance section is the single mathematical authority.
4: `verified-background-1` preserves all ten per-R checks and permits ordinary
5: mathematical compression plus positively checked omitted basic mathlib uses.
6: 
7: ## Admission
8: 
9: An eligible step is correct, routine and local, has all material conditions
10: already available, and needs neither a new hypothesis nor a new core argument.
11: Check mathematical content, not length or familiarity alone. Major tools remain
12: explicit inputs. Wrong quantifiers, unjustified witnesses/limits, hidden project
13: lemmas and inaccessible external citations still block. A source guess is not
14: verification; API difficulty alone is not a mathematical error.
15: 
16: For example, continuity of a pointwise sum follows from the input continuity
17: and the codomain's continuous addition. A reviewer can probe `Continuous.add`
18: and record that application instead of demanding an epsilon-delta proof or an
19: author rewrite. Arbitrary codomains do not supply continuous addition by name.
20: Elementary arithmetic need not display every intermediate chain; a useful short
21: completion can remain an elementary note, with no imported theorem.
22: 
23: ## Record
24: 
25: The reviewer calls `record_background_note` with:
26: 
27: - `id`: local BG001-style ID; `at`: exact `/inference/argument/0/text` pointer;
28: - `kind`: `elementary` or `mathlib`; `fact`: precise statement and conditions;
29: - `grounds`: `{location,reason}` records for actual available inputs,
30:   definitions, parameters or prior in-scope argument;
31: - `justification`: actual correctness/eligibility judgment, not a future TODO;
32: - optional `hint`: short Lean guidance;
33: - for mathlib, `source_id`: the M001-style selector actually checked using
34:   `probe_background`. The controller binds its source/signature/version/evidence;
35:   the reviewer still owns faithful meaning and applicability.
36: 
37: The receipt stores these as `inference_reviews[R].background_notes`; source
38: metadata is case-relative and hash-bound. Existing PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED values
39: remain. PASS with notes describes disclosed routine completion, not unqualified
40: author pre-registration, Lean verification, or success under the old policy.
41: 
42: ## Review and handoff boundary
43: 
44: Local review sees its frozen packet plus logged pinned-mathlib tool responses;
45: it never receives another project proof, author repair history or owner hints.
46: The replay mode and material list disclose this expanded boundary. The actual
47: source probes and tool trace accompany the receipt. Source verification may
48: reuse pinned evidence; it does not require a second model per note.
49: 
50: `nl0.validate` returns the checked note supplement and its hash.
51: `background.effective` creates a derived dependency view adding basic M ports
52: to the appropriate R, without changing author graph bytes or proof paragraphs.
53: At translation entry, retain that supplement and bind its hash in
54: `contract.source.background_supplement_sha256` when notes exist. Include all
55: notes in the local plan; elementary notes need no new theorem root. Mathlib
56: notes become actual library applications, with no new H/axiom/sorry. Audit B
57: checks the same effective inventory and actual Lean closure.
58: 
59: Unchanged note evidence may be inherited with its actual review context. A
60: source extraction changing a consumer with notes requires its affected local
61: review first; the current adapter rejects that case explicitly rather than
62: dropping the notes. Zero extraction and unchanged consumers remain supported.
63: Changed math/conditions return to scoped Audit A; ordinary Lean binding work
64: stays in translation. Historical strict results are preserved, not relabeled.
65: 
66: The interface source also retains the complete `background_supplement`, not
67: just its hash. Plan steps list the relevant qualified note IDs, for example
68: `background_notes:["R004.BG001"]`. Workflow freeze checks the paragraph mapping;
69: local Lean packets receive only their selected notes.

249: ## A3. Structure

258: ## A4. Review every inference
259: 
260: Apply verified-background-1 while retaining every check below. An eligible
261: omitted basic fact receives a positively checked background note and does not
262: fail solely for missing input accounting. Ordinary correct elementary
263: compression needs no exhaustive displayed chain. Substantive missing grounds,
264: conditions, sources or proof still block. The accepted local material includes
265: the version-bound supplement; it cannot be reconstructed silently from memory.

267: First check three closures from the actual text:
268: 
269: - **statement_closure**: input/output statements include every claimed formula,
270:   condition, binder and semantic convention. No producer proof is needed to
271:   understand them. Source notation and inherited equation numbers are not content.
272: - **object_closure**: actual object occurrences map to legitimate declarations
273:   in scope. Compare text to the inventory, not the inventory to itself. Check
274:   input instantiation, witness existence and parameter dependence.
275: - **dependency_closure**: actual factual uses map to direct inputs, prior
276:   in-scope local proofs or fixed logical/calculation steps. An ancestor not
277:   listed as input is unavailable; prior/source proof bodies supply no extra fact.
278: 
279: Then check the six mathematical obligations below. Every check needs a separate
280: `{verdict, notes, evidence, locations}` record with precise packet locations and
281: an explanation. Repeating author notes or generic assurances is not review.
282: 
283: 1. **inputs**: the cited propositions are the actual graph inputs and true
284:    earlier results, original H, or verified sources. They are instantiated
285:    with compatible parameters and definitions.
286: 2. **argument**: every step is justified and sufficient. Explicitly inspect
287:    domain, limits, operator applications, integrability, sign, constants,
288:    uniformity, degeneracies, and selected witnesses where material.
289: 3. **dependency_accounting**: each declared input has an identifiable role;
290:    no additional nontrivial theorem is hidden in “clearly,” an analogy,
291:    a definition, or a convenient abstract interface. Locally derived facts are
292:    permitted only after their derivation. This is accounting for the present
293:    argument, not a claim that its input set is minimal across all proofs.
294:    A named theorem is also an imported fact unless its full required result
295:    is actually proved locally. Explaining why its hypotheses hold is an
296:    application check, not a proof of that theorem. For example, “apply FTC,”
297:    “Fubini applies because the function is integrable,” “compactness gives
298:    uniform continuity,” and “a dominated limit may be integrated” require
299:    declared E/M inputs or complete earlier local proofs of the needed results.
300:    Familiarity, a descriptive theorem name, or inclusion in an author-written
301:    calculation-policy sentence cannot waive this obligation. Ordinary valid textbook compression is allowed for eligible background;
302:    substantive tools and missing arguments still need their actual grounds.
303:    An abstract finite-dimensional, tensor or localization lemma is not
304:    automatically a finite arithmetic identity: inspect its displayed map,
305:    inverse, basis or other derivation, or require the actual declared source.
306: 4. **output**: the derived theorem is exactly the output's full statement,
307:    including quantifier order, assumptions, scope, constants and endpoints.
308: 5. **scope**: temporary assumptions are correctly closed into the implication,
309:    negation, cases, or other allowed rule. Check binder freshness and witness
310:    escape. Introduce/discharge metadata alone is not proof. Do not reclassify
311:    a temporary assumption as an original H.
312: 6. **applicability**: check every E/M obligation using its actual bindings and
313:    input/local proofs, including any proved bridge. For each E application A
314:    record separate binding, per-hypothesis and conclusion reviews and the N
315:    bridge IDs. “The theorem applies” is not a hypothesis mapping.

317: Finally complete **packet_replay**, the tenth check. A fresh context reviews
318: the exact packet, Yui rules and logged pinned-mathlib queries for verified
319: background, without original-source proofs, other R
320: bodies, old NL0, author audit notes or prefilled verdicts. Record actual carrier,

322: Source fidelity is a separate check. Same-context rereading is a diagnostic,

329: queries and source probes for background notes, never arbitrary local files.

332: Use `audit-template` for scaffolds. Every generated verdict starts UNVERIFIED.

1: # Self-containment details
2: 
3: This is the detailed meaning of Audit A's `statement_closure`,
4: `object_closure` and `dependency_closure` requirements. The
5: [shared Audit A section](audit-a.md#shared-mathematical-acceptance-requirements)
6: is the acceptance authority for author and auditor; this annex supplies
7: interpretation and examples, not an independent permission policy.
8: 
9: ## Two boundaries
10: 
11: Accepted NL0 is a complete proof relative to its declared H/E/M roots, frozen
12: logical foundation and version-bound verified background notes. It is not an outline requiring the original manuscript to
13: recover missing definitions, formulas, assumptions, or arguments. E/M statements
14: are fully restated; their primary sources are inspected for provenance, not
15: used to supply unstated premises. The fixed library's own proof dependencies
16: need not be recopied. The target work's internal results must be proved here.
17: 
18: Every R must also be checkable from its packet alone: the complete statements
19: of its direct inputs, their required definitions/declarations, its complete
20: output, its local declarations, and its own argument. Another R's proof body,
21: an ancestor not listed as an input, an ambient original H, an original-source
22: crosswalk, or remembered material is not an additional mathematical resource.
23: Whole-target/source-fidelity checks are separate from this local proof check.
24: Under verified-background-1, local review may additionally verify routine
25: pinned-mathlib facts using logged read-only queries and record them in the
26: receipt. They join this R's effective dependencies, without new H or a graph
27: rewrite. See [background notes](background-notes.md). Mathematical uncertainty
28: still blocks; ordinary correct elementary compression alone does not.
29: 
30: Original theorem conditions are H nodes, including conditions that could be
31: encoded in a refined type. Parameters introduce ambient data/structures, not
32: an ambient stock of original hypotheses. For example, declare a vector and
33: put its required nonzero condition in H; do not write “nonzero vector” in its
34: parameter type and use that condition from an empty input list. The same rule
35: applies to characteristic/range conditions and equations. An R must list every
36: original H it actually uses. Standard structure operations/axioms and the fixed
37: finite-language rules remain available; no new substantive theorem is added.
38: 
39: An output must be understandable and callable without reading its producer's
40: argument. Include the actual equalities/inequalities, binder types, hypotheses,
41: parameter windows, constant dependencies, representatives and a.e./pointwise
42: meaning. Global defined notation can be expanded from the packet. A formula
43: number, theorem name, or paragraph location cannot replace mathematical content.
44: Source locators belong in provenance fields. New mathematical prose uses direct
45: input IDs and previously proved local F IDs, not inherited numbered references.
46: 
47: ## Object closure
48: 
49: For every mathematical object actually appearing in a statement, definition,
50: local declaration, or proof, locate one legitimate declaration:
51: 
52: 1. A frozen parameter, explicit logical primitive, or global D definition.
53:    State its meaning, type/domain and parameter dependence. Global primitives
54:    cover only core typed syntax, not a dictionary of subject-specific objects.
55:    New subjects use the same parameter/definition/local declaration mechanism;
56:    symbol registration never licenses a theorem.
57: 2. A binder inside the current proposition's full statement. Its scope remains
58:    that statement. A variable bound in an input does not become a free object
59:    in the consuming proof; instantiate the statement explicitly.
60: 3. A local declaration before first use, recording its kind, type, exact
61:    declaration, introduction basis, and scope. An arbitrary variable requires
62:    legitimate quantifier introduction; a definition uses already available
63:    objects; a witness requires an input or an earlier local existence proof.
64: 
65: A declaration cannot grant existence, uniqueness, invertibility, regularity,
66: or a desired property merely by naming an object. Those obligations require
67: proof. Any D guard needed to use the object must be a direct R input, not a
68: theorem silently recovered from ancestor closure. Record mutually compatible
69: choices and witness dependence. Temporary assumptions stay inside R and must
70: be correctly discharged. Branch witnesses, local facts and local notation
71: cannot escape their scopes. Export a quantified or conditional statement when
72: needed, rather than a free private name. Global names are reserved; dummy
73: variables may be reused in disjoint local scopes.
74: 
75: ## Dependency closure
76: 
77: Inventory actual factual uses from the prose back to their grounds, not just
78: from an input list forward to a generic `uses` list. Each substantive imported theorem, prior project lemma or original
79: assumption must be a direct input. Eligible omitted basic library uses are
80: recorded as verified audit notes in the effective dependency ledger. A definition supplies meaning, not a theorem. An R output is not its
81: own premise. Adding the desired formula as an unproved input is not a repair.
82: 
83: Explicit local calculations and fully proved intermediate facts may remain
84: inside R. Give a reused local fact a full F statement and identify its earlier
85: derivation and open assumptions. No separate graph vertex is needed for every
86: algebraic equality. A nontrivial imported result cannot be called a local
87: calculation. Substantive reusable lemmas should become N/R pairs; any fact
88: reused by another R must be exported in a complete proposition statement.
89: 
90: The controller owns `spec.logic.calculations` and the small core syntax table
91: (`nl0/scripts/foundations.py`). The clean author tool binds omitted metadata and
92: rejects extra author permissions or task-specific primitives. This fixed
93: language grants no MVT, FTC, Fubini, convergence, compactness or regularity
94: theorem. Such facts need a declared input or an actual local derivation.
95: An author-written permission claim, in any field or prose, has no authority.
96: Ordinary typed arithmetic notation is part of this fixed language: natural
97: numbers, integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers mean their standard
98: structures with usual numerals and operations. Finite calculations include
99: their zero/one laws, such as `a+0=a`, as well as explicit algebra/order
100: derivations. Do not demand a separate E/M for an operation token or an allowed
101: finite calculation. This does not grant calculus, topology or measure theorems.
102: Conversely, inspect an actual displayed local derivation before demanding a
103: duplicate E/M input for its conclusion. A named consequence proved by permitted
104: finite algebra/order steps is not an imported premise. If a local derivation
105: fails, locate its unsupported implication rather than its absent theorem name.
106: 
107: Metadata accounts for the argument but never replaces it. Copying all inputs
108: into a single `uses` record, registering a symbol without declaring it in the
109: proof, or writing a PASS label cannot establish closure.
110: 
111: ## Operational acceptance
112: 
113: 1. Author using the node template. Reverse-check the actual prose for missing
114:    declarations, unexpanded references and unlisted facts before freezing.
115: 2. Generate a packet for each R. The v2 generator supplies no original proof,
116:    producer proofs, provenance file locators, extra ancestor statements or
117:    undeclared ambient H. Direct source contracts and required definitions are
118:    included. Packet hashes bind the mathematical input actually reviewed.
119: 3. Review all closure/inference checks, admitting positively checked routine
120:    background notes under the shared policy. Record concrete packet locations and reasons for every verdict.
121: 4. Perform a fresh local replay with disclosed controlled background lookup. The reviewer gets the skill instructions
122:    and that packet plus logged pinned-mathlib queries, without original proof,
123:    other R bodies, author review
124:    notes, old verdicts, or an answer key. Record the actual carrier, packet hash,
125:    prior exposure and mathematical material read. Skill instructions supply no
126:    extra mathematical premise. Do not falsely claim a same-context rereading
127:    is a fresh replay. This rule does not authorize starting a new external
128:    service or agent; if the required carrier has not been used, keep replay
129:    UNVERIFIED and report that limit.
130:    Prior exposure means known task/proof material supplied or read in earlier
131:    contexts; this is not a claim about unknown pretraining contents. Learned
132:    mathematical knowledge cannot replace a missing declared premise or proof.
133: 5. An ineligible missing declaration, missing statement content, unlisted substantive theorem or need
134:    to look outside the packet blocks acceptance. Record the defect; do not
135:    silently repair it while assigning PASS. Return substantive/structural defects to authoring and review the frozen
136:    revision; eligible background notes need no author rewrite. Routine completion does not require a
137:    separate user interruption for every omission. Distinguish a representation
138:    defect from a substantive mathematical gap under the existing gap policy.
139: 
140: The code rejects explicit malformed references, inventories, scopes, guards
141: and receipts. It does not infer hidden hypotheses from property words in types,
142: or decide theorem applications by matching a list of mathematical names.
143: These semantic obligations apply equally to every subject and remain part of
144: author inspection and Audit A. An omitted inventory entry or unnamed
145: theorem hidden in prose still requires actual semantic review. Freshness and
146: truthful reviewer identity need execution evidence; record shape/hashes cannot
147: authenticate them. No natural-language audit is a Lean kernel certificate.

16: ## Authority and semantics
17: 
18: The isolated authoring carrier offers `check_draft` and `submit_draft`, taking
19: an `artifact` JSON object directly. Prefer these to the compatible older
20: `artifact_json` string wrappers: an additional string-encoding layer is not
21: part of the mathematical format. Both routes execute identical checks.

23: `spec.json` freezes the original full theorem, the conclusion under its declared
24: parameters/hypotheses, the exact H list, global definition pairs, logic policy,
25: source-input hashes, and Lean/mathlib pins. A human must confirm that this
26: specification matches the original problem; string equality cannot establish
27: semantic fidelity. `nl0.json` references this spec by its SHA256 and duplicates
28: none of its definitions or H statements. One separate spec is required per
29: target. Multiple-target decomposition is outside version 2.
30: 
31: Read a derived proposition as a theorem under the original parameters and the
32: H nodes actually used on its derivation path. All additional free variables are
33: locally quantified in its statement; there are no ambient undeclared claims.
34: An unused original H is allowed and reported; do not silently strengthen or
35: weaken the frozen theorem. E/M results retain their general signatures; apply
36: them through explicit bindings and hypothesis checks in the inference.
37: 
38: Graph vertices are propositions and inferences. Edges are generated only as
39: `input proposition -> inference -> output proposition`. An inference requires
40: all inputs. List order is presentation only: a dependency may occur later in
41: the JSON array, provided the graph admits a topological order. Actual circular
42: dependencies, unknown IDs, and disconnected retained branches fail.

44: The isolated authoring carrier also reports a hash-bound machine checkpoint of
45: its latest own draft and actual structural result. After a context reset, resume
46: that candidate with `read_draft`/`base_candidate`; do not claim no draft exists or
47: restart the frozen input accidentally. The checkpoint grants no Audit A verdict.

49: ## Specification fields
50: 
51: Use [the authoring template](../templates/authoring.md) and the complete
52: [model-visible submission example](../templates/submission-example.md). The
53: example explains metadata placeholders and local-witness accounting; it is not
54: a benchmark or proof certification. Required top-level spec fields are:
55: 
56: - `format_version: 2`, `case_id`, `full_target`, `conclusion` (nonempty strings);
57: - `parameters`: records `{symbol, type}`; parameter symbols reserve global names.
58:   Give ambient data types/structures only. Original conditions, ranges and
59:   equations belong in H, not in parameter refinements that would be visible
60:   to every R;
61: - `hypotheses`: records `{id: Hddd, statement, origin}` extracted before authoring;
62: - `definitions`: records `{id: Dddd, symbol, definition, type, depends_on,
63:   requires, binders, objects}`. Each symbol has exactly one global meaning. `depends_on` lists
64:   earlier/resolvable D IDs and is acyclic. `requires` lists proved H/N IDs that
65:   must already be available whenever the definition is used;
66: - `logic`: `{classical: boolean, rules: [names], calculations: [fixed IDs],
67:   primitives: [{symbol, type, meaning}]}`. In the clean author tool, omit
68:   `calculations` and `primitives` to bind the controller's fixed language profile.
69:   Optional calculation IDs are `equality`, `definitions`, `finite_algebra`,
70:   `finite_order`, `finite_sums`. Optional primitive selections may be
71:   `{symbol: ...}`; the controller validates selections and binds the complete
72:   core syntax with exact type/meaning (numerals, number systems and empty-set/top

75:   and conflicting primitive meanings are rejected, not silently accepted;
76: - `pins`: `{lean_version, mathlib_commit, mathlib_root}`; the root is a local
